Studies have shown that early evaluation and treatment can lead to a better outcome. Patients are often first evaluated in their mid-teenage years by a dentist, orthodontist, or oral and maxillofacial surgeon.

All outpatient wisdom tooth surgery is performed with appropriate anesthesia to maximize comfort. Our doctors are trained, licensed, and experienced in providing anesthesia options for oral surgery patients.

note.label: Best timing
note.text: Many patients heal faster and more predictably when wisdom teeth are treated in the teenage years or early twenties, before roots fully mature and jawbone becomes denser.

cards.h2: Limited space can create several long-term concerns.
sub: If there is not enough room for third molars to fully erupt, impacted wisdom teeth can cause problems with gum tissue, neighboring teeth, jaw bone, and future dental stability.

items.title: Infection
body: When there is not enough room for full eruption, gum tissue around a wisdom tooth can become irritated or infected, causing recurrent pain, swelling, and difficulty chewing or swallowing.

items.title: Cyst formation
body: Cysts can develop around impacted wisdom teeth and gradually damage nearby jawbone or teeth. These problems are often harder to treat when removal is delayed.

items.title: Crowding
body: Impacted wisdom teeth may contribute to crowding, especially around the lower front teeth after braces or during early adulthood.

items.title: Adjacent tooth damage
body: If a wisdom tooth is difficult to clean around, the second molar in front of it can be affected by gum disease, bone loss, or decay.

panel.h2: Sedation and monitoring help make the visit calm.
paragraphs: Most patients prefer to be unaware of the experience and choose sedation. At consultation, anesthesia options are reviewed, and the team explains how to prepare for the appointment.
chips: Adult escort needed for the appointment and rest of day
Typical procedure time is about 30 to 60 minutes
Most patients are in the office about 90 minutes

pair.h2: Fasting instructions matter for anesthesia safety.
paragraphs: On the day of surgery, it is important to follow food and drink instructions closely. Having anything in your stomach can increase the risk of anesthetic complications, including nausea and vomiting.

pair.h2: Most post-op changes improve within several days.
paragraphs: Dissolving stitches, gum swelling, and a pulling sensation can be normal. Clear liquids are usually recommended first, with your diet increasing gradually as your body permits.

cta.h2: Have questions before wisdom teeth removal?
paragraphs: We will review your x-rays, discuss anesthesia options, answer your questions, and explain cost and insurance expectations before surgery.

zygomatic-implants.description: Learn how zygomatic implants can provide fixed teeth for patients with severe upper jaw bone loss, often without bone grafting or sinus lift procedures.

hero.lede: Zygomatic implants are designed for patients with severe upper-jaw bone loss who have been told they are not candidates for conventional implants or that dentures are their only option.

intro.h2: A teeth replacement option when upper-jaw bone is limited.
paragraphs: Patients with moderate, advanced, or extreme resorption in the upper jaw may not have enough bone to support conventional dental implants. Zygomatic implants are an alternative to traditional implants and bone grafting in these cases.
Instead of relying only on upper-jaw bone, zygomatic implants attach to the zygoma, or cheekbone. This thick, solid bone can provide stable support for a non-removable replacement appliance.
Because this approach can avoid bone grafting and the lengthy healing period that often follows grafting, implants may be placed immediately for patients who qualify.

note.label: Bone graft alternative
note.text: Zygomatic implants are often considered when bone grafting, sinus lift, or conventional implant treatment would be too limited, lengthy, or unpredictable for the upper jaw.

cards.h2: 3D planning guides precise placement in the cheekbone.
sub: Zygomatic implant placement requires careful planning, advanced imaging, and specialized surgical training. The goal is to create strong support for fixed teeth while avoiding unnecessary grafting whenever possible.

items.title: Consultation and imaging
body: Your team gathers detailed information with advanced technology, including CBCT imaging and 3D planning, so each implant can be positioned with precision.

items.title: Pre-surgical planning
body: The scans help your surgeon understand bone quality, sinus anatomy, restoration needs, and whether traditional implants will be combined with zygomatic implants.

items.title: Implant placement
body: Long implant screws are anchored in the zygoma, the strong cheekbone near the sinus. Often, two zygomatic implants are used with two to four traditional implants in the front jaw.

items.title: Single-surgery treatment
body: If teeth need to be removed first, extractions may be completed during the same surgery before zygomatic implant placement.

panel.h2: A fixed solution without the usual grafting timeline.
paragraphs: For the right patient, zygomatic implants can provide fully functional teeth, reduce the need for grafting, and streamline treatment into a shorter, more comfortable path.
chips: Fixed teeth can often be loaded immediately
No bone grafting for many patients
No sinus lift in many cases

pair.h2: This treatment requires specialized expertise.
paragraphs: The surgical skill involved in placing zygomatic implants requires extensive training and experience. Our doctors have formal training in zygomatic placement and plan each case carefully.

pair.h2: Most patients are surprised by recovery.
paragraphs: IV sedation and anti-inflammatory medications help support comfort. Any discomfort is often similar to bone grafting recovery, with mild bruising and pain usually managed with over-the-counter medications.

cta.h2: Find out if zygomatic implants are possible.
paragraphs: We will review your imaging, bone condition, and goals to determine whether zygomatic implants can restore function and confidence.
